project_name: Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems
initial_requirements: The Ministry of Home Affairs needs a Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems application to improve day-to-day police work and support better crime investigation and criminal detection. The system will be used by investigating officers, records staff, and citizens. It should provide an initial foundation for registering complaints, supporting investigations, and exchanging relevant information between police units and the public.

GAMMA-J needs a web store that enables people who are new to online commerce to set up and operate an online retail business. Store owners and sales personnel should be able to manage products and customer accounts, while customers should be able to browse the available products, maintain a shopping cart, and place orders through the store.

A university needs a Unified University Inventory System that combines the inventory databases of three faculties and makes the integrated inventory available through a secure web interface. University, faculty, and department staff need to manage assets such as rooms, software licences, and equipment, while other users should be able to request assets or reserve spaces for approval by the appropriate administrative level.

Qheadache is intended to be a standalone computerized puzzle game for people ranging from young beginners to adult players. Players use a graphical board to move blocks and solve a predefined challenge. The application should support normal play and retain useful information about a player's progress and results, such as time, actions, and scores.

A stock trading platform needs a Central Trading System as one subsystem within a larger trading environment. It must receive trading instructions from the client-facing service, distinguish among different instruction types, and match compatible stock orders according to the applicable trading rules. The subsystem must also communicate the resulting trading information to other parts of the platform and allow authorized system managers to inspect its information.

The Southwest Florida Water Management District needs a GIS-based Water Use Tracking System for District employees and external customers. The system should support spatial and temporal analysis of regulatory and resource-management data, particularly permitted and actual water use. It is intended to replace inconsistent manual and semi-automated analyses and help staff evaluate water-use trends and assess the effects of management rules.

KeePass Password Safe is intended to help users manage many passwords without repeatedly reusing or memorizing them. It should store passwords, usernames, email accounts, URLs, and related notes in an encrypted database protected by a master credential. Users also need a practical way to organize and use the stored entries while keeping the database portable between computers.

NJIT needs a secure distance-learning environment that helps professors communicate and work with students online. Virtual-EDU should provide a classroom-like portal where enrolled users can communicate individually or in groups, share and collaborate on learning materials, and participate in online course activities. Administrators will also need to manage the learning environment and its enrolled users.

The Gemini observatory needs an integrated software environment for controlling its telescopes and scientific instruments. Observing astronomers should be able to acquire astronomical data and assess its quality without having to manage the low-level details of individual subsystems. The system must support users with different operational responsibilities and provide consistent access to telescope status and observing functions from appropriate local or remote facilities.

The Energy Management System is intended to monitor and manage heating and cooling activity independently of the equipment it supervises. It should evaluate temperature conditions, determine when heating or cooling resources are needed, and report important operating events. Users need a reliable way to initialize the system, review its status, and understand situations such as temperature limits or unavailable equipment.

MultiMahjong is a computer version of Mahjong for both networked and standalone play. Up to four people should be able to join a shared game through client applications connected to a game server. When fewer human players are available, the application should provide computer-controlled opponents so that a user can still start and complete a valid game.

Owners and users of a computing cluster need a scheduler that allocates processing resources according to user-oriented quality-of-service goals. Libra will receive submitted batch jobs from an existing cluster management system and schedule them using information such as each user's budget and deadline. It should select suitable execution resources and enforce the resulting allocation while the surrounding platform remains responsible for receiving and dispatching jobs.

Pecan Springs Elementary School needs a web-based learning game that helps sixth-grade students improve their fraction-solving skills. Students should answer fraction questions as part of an interactive game and receive feedback based on their performance. The project should also provide a common web menu through which students and teachers can access Space Fractions alongside related educational games.

Building operators and facilities managers need an automated diagnostic tool that can detect and identify faults in HVAC components such as chillers and cooling-tower subsystems. The tool should combine sensed operating data with equipment specifications and configuration information, then present diagnostic results that help users monitor equipment condition. Service technicians and energy-service personnel may also use it during maintenance or remote supervision.

Scientists need a grid-based software environment for conducting biogeochemical modeling with weather observations and remote computing resources. The system should let scientific users manage input data, run surface-weather interpolation and ecosystem simulations, visualize results, and manage generated outputs through a graphical interface. It should support secure, reliable use of distributed computing resources without requiring users to handle the underlying grid infrastructure directly.

Tarrant County needs an integrated justice capability to improve the administration of indigent defense services and information sharing across the criminal justice community. The system should help the Office of Attorney Appointments receive and process requests for appointed counsel, obtain relevant defendant and case information, coordinate attorney appointments, and notify the people and justice organizations involved in each request.

The Federal Highway Administration needs the Clarus system to collect, quality-control, and share environmental and road-condition observations from transportation networks. Transportation agencies, observation-system operators, weather-service providers, and researchers should be able to contribute or use the data. The system is intended to support safer road operations, timely responses to weather, and improved forecasting through an integrated source of surface transportation observations.

Public health organizations need an outbreak management system to support investigation, monitoring, analysis, and reporting during disease outbreaks, bioterrorism incidents, and other health events. Investigators should be able to collect information about cases, contacts, exposures, specimens, and interventions, connect related entities and events, and use the resulting information to identify and contain a health threat while protecting sensitive data.

Transportation agencies need the next generation of the Pontis Bridge Management System to manage bridge inventories and related improvement projects. Authorized users should be able to find and review bridge and project information, support inspection activities, and work with the data needed for planning and analysis. The system must accommodate different agency users and preserve appropriate control over operational and administrative information.

The National Library of Medicine needs a digital repository for collection materials produced by existing and future digitization projects. Members of the public and NIH staff should be able to discover and view permitted materials, while authorized library staff need to create and maintain metadata, ingest or update digital objects, and manage their long-term preservation. Access may vary according to rights and user circumstances.

Developers building multi-agent systems need an expanded agentMom framework that provides reusable communication capabilities for agents and their conversations. Agents should be able to communicate with one recipient, selected groups, or all agents on a local network, join and leave communication groups, and choose whether messages require protection. The new framework must remain usable with applications based on the existing agentMom environment.

ABC Paint needs a web application to help customers and distributors move from an old paint numbering scheme to a new product line without losing continuity in color selection. Users should be able to translate previous paint numbers, explore available colors, and find suitable products near a chosen color. Authorized staff also need to maintain the colors and product information offered through the application.

Marie Stopes International Uganda needs a Voucher Management Unit System for an output-based health program that subsidizes services through patient vouchers. Program staff should be able to create and distribute vouchers, record sales and treatment claims, validate claims from service providers, arrange eligible reimbursements, and monitor program results. The system should reduce manual processing while helping staff identify questionable or potentially fraudulent claims.

A child care center needs a web-based management system that reduces administrative work and lets employees share information through a central database. Administrators should be able to register families and manage enrollment, classroom capacity, and waiting lists, while authorized staff need support for routine activities such as tracking child immunizations, processing invoices, and producing information for customers and center operations.

project_name: Marvel Electronics and Home Entertainment E-Store
initial_requirements: Marvel Electronics and Home Entertainment needs an online store to support the sale, distribution, and marketing of electronic products. Customers should be able to browse categorized product information, search the catalogue, and configure products from available components before ordering. The business also needs a way to present detailed product information and manage the customer-facing sales experience through the store.

project_name: University of Puget Sound Courseware System
initial_requirements: The University of Puget Sound needs a courseware system that better supports its instructional and educational practices. Students, professors, and system administrators should be able to manage courses, assignments, learning materials, discussions, and grades through a coherent online environment. The project should also improve collaboration and access to course content while allowing the university to refine the system as stakeholder needs become clearer.

State executive-branch agencies need a shared enterprise service for e-mail, messaging, calendars, and contacts. The service should support everyday communication and collaboration for agency users while allowing administrators to provision accounts, manage shared information, and apply organization-wide controls. The initiative is intended to meet confidentiality, privacy, security, retention, and operational needs while reducing the cost and duplication of separately supported agency systems.

Construction Junction needs a categorized inventory management system for staff who receive, organize, and sell donated materials. Users should be able to navigate departments and item categories, view individual inventory records, and add or update appropriate stock and unique items. The system must keep operational inventory information aligned with the organization's point-of-sale activities while supporting different staff responsibilities.

Georgia Library PINES needs improved management and reporting capabilities within its shared integrated library system. Library managers, directors, staff, and consortium administrators should be able to analyze collection use, branch capacity, patron interests, staff workflows, and financial activity across participating libraries. The system should support both local decision-making and consortium-wide oversight without disrupting the operational services used by patrons and library staff.

Users need a video-search application that can query multiple websites at once for streaming sources and downloadable video listings. A user should be able to search for a specific title or genre, choose which types of sources to include, compare organized results, and retain useful favorites. System maintainers also need a way to control which external sites participate in searches.

UK fishing vessel masters and owners need an onboard electronic logbook that replaces paper recording for regulated fishing activity. The system should capture required logbook, transhipment, and landing information and transmit compliant reports to the appropriate fisheries administration. It should help vessel operators review and submit accurate records while accommodating relevant data supplied by other onboard systems.

Home residents need a DigitalHome system for monitoring and controlling devices that affect security, temperature, humidity, lighting, and small appliances. General users should be able to manage their home environment through a personal web interface, while designated master users and technicians need additional configuration capabilities. The system must coordinate information and commands between its web services and the sensors and controllers installed in the home.

project_name: DII Common Operating Environment XML Services
initial_requirements: Defense mission and support applications need common XML services within the Defense Information Infrastructure operating environment. The services should let authorized users and applications register shared terms and structures, define reusable XML schemas, and create or consume XML documents. They should also provide vendor-independent access to distributed information so applications can exchange and manage data without depending on a particular physical database implementation.

Military services need a common Tactical Control System for operating different current and future unmanned aerial vehicles and their payloads. Operators should be able to plan and control missions, monitor aircraft and payload status, receive and process sensor information, and distribute imagery and other mission products. The system must also exchange tasking and operational information with the wider command-and-control environment.

NASA's X-38 Crew Return Vehicle needs Fault Tolerant System Services for its redundant flight-critical computer. The software should provide mission applications with dependable scheduling, communication, time, memory, and system-support capabilities while isolating them from underlying processor and operating-system details. It must also detect and isolate faults, coordinate redundant resources, and help the vehicle continue operating safely when individual computing components fail.

People using public terminals and kiosks need an Accesspoint that connects them to context-sensitive information and services. The terminal should support graphical, spoken, and other interaction modes so users can move between them without losing their current task. It should guide occasional users through conversations, adapt to the immediate context, and remain understandable and stable despite user mistakes or network problems.

Traffic-management organizations in the Dallas-Fort Worth region need a center-to-center network that connects otherwise dissimilar traffic systems. Participating agencies should be able to contribute and share traffic conditions, incidents, and field-device status through a common repository. The network should also support coordinated control of roadside devices and provide accessible map-based traffic information to agencies that do not operate a full traffic management center.

Wind-power operators need a standardized communication system for remotely supervising and operating turbines supplied by different vendors. The system should transfer measurements, status information, alarms, and other plant data to authorized operational applications and carry commands or settings back to individual turbines or wind-farm controllers. It must serve different authorized parties while keeping communication failures from disrupting the safe local operation of the plant.

The Mars Express ASPERA-3 science team needs a ground data system that processes and preserves telemetry from the mission's particle and field instruments. The facility should acquire incoming spacecraft data, transform it into products suitable for scientific analysis, distribute those products to the project team, and provide recent information for public viewing. Validated products must also be retained and delivered for long-term scientific archiving.

Researchers developing high-assurance software need a platform-independent graphical interface for the High Assurance Transformation System. Users should be able to prepare transformation applications, invoke proven transformations on abstract programs, and inspect or manipulate the resulting output without working directly with the underlying command-oriented services. The interface should make experimentation with semantics-preserving program transformation more accessible while retaining confidence in the transformed results.

project_name: Number Portability Administration Center Service Management System
initial_requirements: Telecommunications service providers need a shared administration system for moving customers' telephone numbers between provider networks. The system should receive information from the old and new providers, validate and coordinate their requests, activate agreed routing changes, and distribute updated portability data to participating networks. Operations personnel also need transaction history, conflict handling, reporting, and audit capabilities to keep provider records synchronized.

project_name: Swift X-Ray Telescope Control Processor Flight Software
initial_requirements: NASA's Swift observatory needs flight software for the control processor of its X-Ray Telescope, which helps investigate gamma-ray bursts and their afterglows. The software should receive and dispatch instrument commands, maintain the telescope's operating state, acquire and process detector data, and prepare scientific products for transmission. It must also monitor its own operation, report problems, and support recovery from faults in the space environment.

The Expanded Very Large Array needs an operations system for configuring and monitoring its radio-astronomy correlator and processing the resulting data stream in real time. Scientists and engineers should be able to inspect system health and observational data, while the software assembles and transforms correlator output into usable results for downstream storage and analysis. The system should identify faults and recover automatically where practical.

European card-issuing authorities need a shared TACHOnet service to coordinate driver smart-card requests across participating member organizations. Users should be able to ask one or more members about the possible delivery or status of cards, receive standardized replies, and follow each request through completion. The service should also manage access rights, alert participants when expected replies are late, and provide operational statistics.

project_name: JSE Money Market ISIN Issuance Service
initial_requirements: The JSE Securities Exchange South Africa needs an electronic service for issuing identifiers for dematerialized money-market instruments. Money Market Forum participants should be able to submit requests through STRATE to create, amend, or delete ISIN codes, with the JSE returning identifiers quickly enough to support same-day trading, clearing, and settlement. The service should reduce manual processing while preserving controlled and reliable market records.

Philips Digital Systems Laboratories wants an instant-messaging application that demonstrates communication through its interactive television platform. Television users should sign in with an existing account, see which friends are online and what programs they are watching, exchange text messages, manage their presence and nickname, and maintain a buddy list. Users should also be able to block contacts and receive visible notifications when messages arrive.

California Department of Transportation District 11 needs to replace the aging I-15 Reversible Lane Control System application. Traffic operators should be able to open and close reversible lanes for peak periods and special events, observe field-device and overall system status, issue control commands, configure operations, and generate reports. Authorized users and connected transportation systems should also receive relevant operational data through controlled local or remote access.

Researchers working with biological data need a Grid 3D application that turns supplied datasets into an interactive three-dimensional view. Identifiers, investigators, and demonstrators should be able to load data, inspect individual or multiple points, retrieve associated information, and manipulate the grid by rotating, moving, and zooming it. The application should present graphical or textual results appropriate to each user's analytical or demonstration task.

Researchers need a standalone application for playing and extending combinatorial games based on triangulations. Players with varying technical experience should be able to choose among several game types and play alone, against computer-controlled opponents, or with another person through an accessible graphical interface. Game developers should also be able to define new games and make them available without modifying the original application.

Project ZNIX aims to provide an object-based, application-independent framework for retrieving and manipulating personal information. Casual users should be able to archive diverse information, organize it through relationships and hierarchies they find meaningful, and add, change, remove, categorize, or back up items without disrupting that organization. The framework should also expose services that allow compatible client applications to work with the same information.

USDA Agricultural Research Service needs a centralized system for watershed research data that is currently managed separately at individual sites. Watershed staff should upload and maintain standardized water, soil, land-management, conservation, and economic data, while researchers and approved public users can search, analyze, visualize, download, and report integrated datasets. Access must reflect the responsibilities and confidentiality limits of different user groups.

The Oregon University System wants to update the Get Real website to encourage high-school students to consider computer science degrees and careers. The site should provide a teen-friendly path through university course information, career guidance, stories from computing professionals, and practical preparation advice. It should serve both students already interested in computing and college-bound students who may need more context or encouragement.

project_name: VII Data Use Analysis and Processing System
initial_requirements: The Michigan Department of Transportation needs a prototype Data Use Analysis and Processing system to evaluate how connected-vehicle and related data can support safety, traffic management, asset management, winter operations, and planning. The system should collect continuously arriving vehicle, traffic, weather, and traveler information, consolidate it, transform it into useful outputs, and communicate unified information to transportation agencies and the public.

Content delivery network providers need a software infrastructure that lets otherwise independent CDNs cooperate when demand exceeds local capacity. Providers should be able to discover potential peers, negotiate resource-sharing relationships and policies, replicate content, redirect user requests, and exchange load and accounting information. The arrangement should adapt to changing demand, protect information each provider chooses not to share, and support orderly expansion or termination.

Ejada needs a supply chain management system to coordinate delivery of its information-technology products, consulting, and related services. Staff should be able to manage customer service, procurement, supplier and material selection, product development, manufacturing flow, physical distribution, outsourcing, and partnerships. The system should also help the company assess cost, productivity, assets, service, and quality performance across the supply chain.

Vrije Universiteit Brussel needs a Publications Management System for storing bibliographic records and full publication texts. Users with different roles should be able to search, upload, download, correct, and moderate publication information according to their access rights. The system should extract bibliographic details from documents, support bulk imports, and help reconcile alternative names that refer to the same author or institution.

project_name: Security and Privacy Requirements Analysis Tool
initial_requirements: Requirements and privacy analysts need SPRAT, a collaborative workbench for aligning web-system requirements with privacy and security policies. Users should be able to capture goals, scenarios, policies, requirements, and legal-compliance information; trace goals back to their source policies; organize them with flexible classifications; and compare analyses produced by different people. Access should vary for administrators, project managers, analysts, and guests.

European railways need a standardized digital mobile radio system for interoperable ground-to-train and ground-based communications. Train drivers, trackside workers, station and depot staff, and operational personnel should be able to make individual, group, broadcast, and emergency calls and exchange operational data. Radios should support role-specific use, functional addressing, network changes, and priority handling without disrupting higher-priority railway communications.

European railways need a common train-control system that helps drivers operate safely across lines using different levels of trackside and radio support. The onboard system should supervise train and shunting movements, present relevant train and movement information, prevent unauthorized movement where required, and manage transitions between operating levels. Driver confirmation, braking intervention, and interaction with national train-control functions require further definition.

NOAA needs the NPOESS Data Exploitation system to turn polar-orbiting satellite observations into products for operational, climate, and other civilian users. The system should receive source data, generate standard and NOAA-specific products, package and distribute them to authorized customers, and deliver selected products to the long-term archive. It should also support registration, order status, product assistance, integrity monitoring, and continuity during failures.

The Gaia science-processing community needs a fast simulator that can generate catalog, auxiliary, intermediate, and statistically representative final-mission data for Gaia instruments. Users should be able to select the processing stage and relevant error models, produce large simulated datasets without running the full telemetry and mission-database chain, and deliver results compatible with the wider Gaia processing environment as scientific models evolve.

project_name: King County Library System Administration Module
initial_requirements: King County Library System needs a central administration module for its multi-branch Integrated Library System. System administrators should be able to configure library processes, manage users, groups, and privileges, monitor and troubleshoot servers, databases, applications, services, and interfaces, coordinate software updates, and protect operational data through backup and recovery. The module must support centralized administration without disrupting daily library services.

Scientists and software engineers need a Model Manager that automates the setup and operation of computational model jobs across one or more clusters. Users should be able to configure, schedule, submit, monitor, stop, restart, and resume operational, research, post-processing, or existing scripted jobs. The system should manage nodes and choose execution resources while still allowing experienced users to request a particular cluster when necessary.

Computer users need a cross-platform graphical file and archive manager that brings multiple open-source compression utilities behind one consistent interface. Users should be able to create, update, extract, inspect, split, join, compare, and securely delete files or archives, apply checksums, and protect archives with credentials. Settings should accommodate different preferences, while both inexperienced and advanced users can access appropriate management capabilities.

European businesses need a Virtual Company Dossier service that helps them prove eligibility for public procurement across national borders. Economic operators should be able to identify required evidence, obtain and validate attestations, compile them into a dossier package, and submit it to contracting authorities. Authorities need to authenticate, receive, translate, and view the package while national criteria and evidence are mapped to shared European requirements.

Web-archiving institutions need an expanded WARC Tools suite for managing large collections of archived web content. Archivists and engineers should be able to configure and run migrations from ARC to WARC, repackage collections, inspect and browse records, produce reports, detect duplicates, and verify content and metadata after conversion. The tools should support collaborative deployment and testing across institutions and scale to large collection batches.

Computer users need a graphical partition editor for creating, deleting, resizing, moving, checking, copying, and labeling disk partitions and their file systems. The application should make these operations accessible to casual users while preserving data during supported changes and working with common storage configurations. It should be usable either from an installed environment or from bootable media when the resident operating system is unavailable.

Small and medium businesses need Mashbot to manage their presence across multiple social networks through a consistent service. Staff should be able to connect external accounts, prepare campaigns, schedule content for simultaneous publication, manage contributor, approver, and publisher roles, respond to audience activity, and monitor keywords and campaign history. The service should reduce the effort required to coordinate marketing and customer engagement across changing platforms.

Users need a free graphical tool for manipulating PDF documents without altering their original input files. They should be able to split documents, merge selected files or sections, extract pages, rotate or reorder pages, alternate pages from different documents, and compose new documents visually. The tool should also save reusable work environments and offer a command-line path for recurring or automated operations.
